title: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
summary: Glanzmann thrombasthenia means platelets, the blood cells that help stop bleeding, cannot stick together properly. People bruise easily and can have nosebleeds, gum bleeding or heavy periods.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the same gene (ITGA2B or ITGB3) from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has Glanzmann thrombasthenia. A specialist team helps plan for bleeding, surgery, dental work and periods, and treatments can help stop bleeding.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has Glanzmann thrombasthenia. Could I be a carrier?
Can Glanzmann thrombasthenia skip a generation?
What does a test for Glanzmann thrombasthenia involve?
card_summary: Platelets can't stick together properly, so bleeding lasts longer. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Bleeding lasts longer; a specialist team helps plan care.
care: Specialist haematology and bleeding disorder clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
